I am Aditya Rayilla, an intern posted\u0026nbsp;in medicine department and one of the important terms of getting the internship completion is to complete my log book with my online log of what I learn during the course of my duties.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003ELately we've been getting alot of CNS cases in our hospital, but most of the time we identify the etiology depending on the history and examination, here is a case that shows an ambiguity in diagnosis as the case history points towards one type of a lesion and the examination towards another.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHere is the case presentation of a 40 YO lady with quadriparesis (predominantly paraparesis of lower limbs)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECase History\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ec\/o difficulty in walking since 20days and weakness of both upper limbs\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHOPI: pt was a\/a 20 days ago after which she had a trauma due to slippage of footwear while working in an agricultural field, immediately after fall, pt was unable to stand and nearby workers lifted her and made her sit on a chair. After a while she could walk by herself to home\u0026nbsp; slowly and there after she was unable to sit and stand. She also had dragging type of pain in both the Lower limbs and tingling sensarions of both the Upper Limbs. From then she was unable to walk without support.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/O difficulty in mixing food (rice)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eno h\/o bowel and bladder incontinence\/ seizure episode\/ syncopal attacks\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eno h\/o palpitations\/sob\/pedal edema\/ decreased urine output\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eno h\/o fever\/vomitings\/loosestools\/cough\/cold\/dyspesia\/nasal regurgitation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHISTORY OF PAST ILLNESS\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPast h\/o seizures 2 yeaes back, on oxcarbazepine 300mg\/po\/BD.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ept underwent consultation in khammam for weaknwss, where she was told she was suffering through hypokalmeia for which she received oral correction and discharged.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;no h\/o\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDM, HTN, CAD, ASTHMA, TB, ANTIBIOTICS, HORMONES, RADIATION, BLOOD TRANSFUSION, SURGERIES.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EGeneral examination:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPallor ABSENT\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIcterus absent\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo cyanosis clubbing lymphademopathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDehydration Absent\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETemp Afebrile\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBp 90\/60mm hg\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPr\u0026nbsp; 3.38millions\/cumm\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPLATELET COUNT 3.66\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESMEAR\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENormocytic normochromic\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELeucocytosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdequate in number and distribution\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHEMOPARASITES No hemoparesites seen\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELight Microscopy\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENormocytic normochromic blood\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Epicture\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ewith leucocytosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAMORPHOUS DEPOSITS Nil\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUREA 39\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E#CREATININE 1.3 mg\/dl\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EURIC ACID 3.7\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECALCIUM 10.0\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPHOSPHOROUS 3.8\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESODIUM 143mEq\/L\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPOTASSIUM 3.9mEq\/L\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECHLORIDE104mEq\/L\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHCV- NEGATIVE\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHbsAG NEGATIVE\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHIV NON REACTIVE\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECASE ANALYSIS:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003EIn this case, the case history provides us that the onset of quadriparesis is of a sudden onset in origin which points towards any sort of damage to the cord as in cervical myelopathy or a myelopathy at the lumbar region, if this was the case then it would've presented as a UMN i.e the reflexes would've been exagerated and the tone would've been increased i.e hypertonia. But as we can see through the examination the tone was decreased in the lower limb, gait showed buckling and there was areflexia seen, due to this ambiguity, the neurologist had suggested an MRI. After the MRI and referral from the orthopedician it was concluded that the cause of the quadriparesis was more of an LMN porbably of a peripheral neurpathy type rather than of a myelopathy originated quadriparesis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003EThe patient was discharged as their was no progression nor there was any retrogression and then requested to follow up after a few days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-weight: bold;\"\u003ETAKE HOME LESSON:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci style=\"\"\u003EIn general in the case of a CNS anomaly according to our neurologist the case history plays a major role in identifying the cause of the lesion which has to be confirmed through the examination. But sometimes the inability of the patient to recall the exact sequence of events or to express their problem leaves us with an ambiguous situation. The MRI had suggested us that there were vertebral problems, but the cns examination and after an orthopedician referral it was concluded that the Quadriparesis however is not linked to the abnormalities in the anatomy of the vertebrae which in turn could have caused a myelopathy. Thus it is important to give equal importance to the case history, examination and as well as the radiological evidence we acquire.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHere is a link to the investigations, videos and pictures related to the case\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/drive.google.com\/folderview?id=12ta0Xiuvslsg2V_kCbOowBh3s_J5DJ24\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThank
